Search, navigate, and manage OpenCode sessions from the TUI, with an experimental
OpenCode Desktop interface. Navigator combines
Search Everything, task and subagent views, skills, MCP presets, and quick actions
with a configurable sidebar.

![OpenCode Navigator](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/01-hero-sidebar.png)

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for release-by-release changes.

## Features

- Theme-aware session title with the session creation date
- First-run setup guide with interactive section settings
- Collapsible Todo section with status filters, grouped tasks and progress; OpenCode 2 follows the host's native Todo history, while OpenCode 1.x retains supported priority indicators
- Active subagent list with live statuses and click-to-open navigation, including dev-team workers running in separate local processes
- Compact, searchable workspace skill list with user-wide favorites and groups, recent skills, source details, and click-to-confirm slash commands
- Configurable host quick actions, including OpenCode 1.x's auto-approve toggle and OpenCode 2.x's Permissions settings, with user-wide bookmarks and availability reasons
- Live LSP connection status with error-first sorting and badges that reveal server names in place
- Searchable MCP section with live radio-style connection controls
- Click any MCP row to connect or disconnect it
- Connect or disconnect every eligible MCP server with per-server progress and failed-only retry
- Save named MCP state presets and apply them from the MCP section heading
- Optionally link a layout preset with an MCP preset and apply both through one workspace-profile preview
- Persist enabled and disabled MCP server states globally or per worktree and reapply them between sessions
- Keep favorite MCP servers first across workspaces
- Organize MCP servers into user-wide custom groups while retaining assignments for servers absent from the current workspace
- Search Everything in a keyboard-first modal with category tabs and fuzzy results
- Show or hide each sidebar section independently
- Hide the session title or its creation date independently in OpenCode 1.x without losing the settings control
- Configure section visibility and order from the sidebar settings button
- Open Settings → About for the running version, update checks, versioned release history, and editable GitHub Bug reports
- Separate adjacent sections with quiet theme-aware dividers instead of background cards
- Save visibility, expansion, and order globally or for the current worktree
- Copy the selected scope's layout and MCP states as versioned JSON, then validate and preview imports
- Focus the sidebar with `Ctrl+Shift+F`, then navigate with arrows or `j`/`k`
- Open sidebar shortcut mode with `Ctrl+Shift+B`; press `h` to toggle the panel, `c` to check Navigator updates, or `u` to check and confirm an update
- Scan an icon-led shortcut hint with highlighted keys, separate navigation/update groups, and a clear Escape action; narrow terminals and Text fallback use the same controls
- Optionally open new sessions directly in an empty chat with the sidebar, skipping Home on startup and from New session
- Keep OpenCode's compact footer while showing host and Navigator versions with independent update indicators; click a version label or its update icon to confirm an in-place update through the current installation method and scope

Todo starts expanded. Subagents, skills, quick actions, LSP, and MCP start
collapsed. Use `Save current layout as default` in sidebar settings to reuse the
current visible/hidden, expanded/collapsed, and ordering states in new sessions.

**Only the latest stable release in each major line is supported: OpenCode
1.19.5 and 2.2.6.** Both have separate real-host checks. Older releases are not
part of the supported compatibility matrix. The 2.2 integration uses OpenTUI 0.8
and public host caches, events, keymap layers, and client APIs while retaining
the separate 1.x adapter. See [Host API boundaries](HOST_API.md) for remaining
capability gaps and removal conditions. On OpenCode 2, Navigator reads the same native Todo history as
the host sidebar, including completed `todowrite` calls and the current revert
boundary. Viewing Todo needs no Navigator server plugin. OpenCode 2.1 exposes
content and four statuses, without priorities or direct Todo CRUD. LSP is hidden on 2.x while retaining Subagents,
Skills, Quick Actions, MCP, Search, settings, and presets. All TUI interface icons use Nerd Font glyphs by
default (Codicons for controls, keyboard symbols for hints, language logos for LSP). Use a Nerd Fonts v3
terminal font, or select **Settings → Behavior → Icon style → Text fallback**.
The switch applies to the entire interface, including Quick Actions, search
tabs, section headings, statuses, favorites, and dialogs.
Components read the live style through the shared icon context; host-mounted
and nested dialogs inherit the same context through the dialog adapter.
Highlighted rows, tabs, and buttons use rounded ends in Nerd Font mode;
multiline selections use inverse corner masks over a solid background from the additional
**OpenCode Navigator Corners** fallback font. Installing that font is required
for rounded multiline selections; Nerd Fonts alone do not contain these four
custom glyphs. Without it, disable **Multiline corner font** in Behavior: Nerd Font
icons and single-line rounded controls remain enabled, while multiline highlights
become clean rectangles. Text fallback changes all icons as well. Rounded edges
stay inside the control's padding and remain clickable.
Navigator uses the full available sidebar slot width; the current OpenCode TUI
fixes the outer panel at 42 columns. Long preset labels are truncated to keep the
MCP heading and server count on one line.

## Interface tour

The sidebar title keeps the session creation date visible without a redundant
status icon. Todo and live Subagents remain readable while the rest of the
session stays uncluttered. Filters expose active and finished tasks, live
workers, and recent failures without mixing their states:

![Active Todo tasks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/02-todo-active.png)

![Subagent errors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/05-subagents-errors.png)

Skills, Quick Actions, compact LSP badges, MCP controls, favorites, filters, and
muted section dividers share the same narrow sidebar:

![Quick Actions and LSP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/07-quick-actions-lsp.png)

![MCP sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/08-mcp-sidebar.png)

MCP groups are managed from **Settings → Sections → MCP → Groups**. Favorites
remain in a leading bucket; custom groups and their servers sort alphabetically.
Assignments can select an existing group or open an input to create a new one.
Click a group heading (including Favorites or Ungrouped), or focus it and press
`Enter`, to connect its remaining eligible servers. Once none need connecting,
the same control disconnects its connected servers. This affects the full group
even when a filter or item limit hides some rows; failed operations retain the
usual retry control. The heading has no action label: its radio-style icon is
filled only when every server in the group is connected, empty if any still
needs connecting, and pending while the group changes.

![MCP group manager](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/31-mcp-groups.png)

![MCP error details](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/32-mcp-error.png)

Manage Skill groups from **Settings → Sections → Skills → Groups**. Favorites
stay first, named groups sort alphabetically, and Ungrouped stays last. Groups
belong to each Skill's exact source path, so assignments survive when a Skill
is absent from the current workspace. Filters and Search Everything also match
group names; choosing a group heading never runs its Skills.

Rows beneath group headings are indented in Todo, Subagents, Skills, and MCP.
Skill, MCP, and Quick Action rows reserve a leading bookmark control: unselected
bookmarks appear on hover or keyboard focus, while favorites stay visible.
Labels do not shift when the control appears. MCP server status icons align with
their group status icons, including when a server has an error detail control.

![Skill group manager](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/38-skill-groups.png)

Search Everything preserves one query across Skills, Subagents, MCP, and Actions:

![Search Everything skills](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/09-search-skills.png)

![Search Everything MCP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/11-search-mcp.png)

![Navigator settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/13-settings-sections.png)

![Layout preset preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/20-layout-preset-preview.png)

The preview separates supported layout/MCP changes from future fields that will

![Settings import preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/St1ggy/opencode-navigator/main/screenshots/34-settings-import-preview.png)

## Installation

### OpenCode 1.x

Install the plugin for the current project:

```sh
opencode plugin opencode-navigator
```

Use `--global` to install it for every project:

```sh
opencode plugin --global opencode-navigator
```

`opencode plug` is an alias for `opencode plugin`.

### OpenCode 2.x

Install Navigator through the OpenCode 2 plugin manager:

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-navigator
```

This installs the package and adds it to the `plugins` array in the global
`~/.config/opencode/cli.json`. The equivalent configuration is:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/v2/cli.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-navigator"]
}
```

OpenCode 2.x CLI plugins are global terminal settings; there is no project-local
`cli.json`. Navigator replaces the `sidebar.content` slot, so no built-in sidebar
plugin overrides are required. OpenCode validates `cli.json` strictly, so keep it
within the linked schema and restart OpenCode after changing it.

OpenCode 2's built-in Todo tool is opt-in. When its effective configuration
disables the tool, Navigator offers **Enable Todo…** in the section and
**Enable native Todo** in the command palette. Choose an existing discovered
server configuration file, review `experimental.todo → true`, then confirm
**Enable Todo**. Cancel and Escape preserve the file. Navigator retains JSONC
comments, formatting and unrelated settings, and checks for changed files,
configuration sources, sessions and workspaces before writing.

The check uses the host configuration, not the presence or absence of tasks.
An enabled empty list therefore says **No tasks yet** without another enable
offer. Configuration read failures have their own Retry action. Remote file
operations stay on the connected server; no model or Todo mutation is used for
setup. Refresh or restart OpenCode if a saved flag has not yet been applied.
See [Host API boundaries](HOST_API.md) for precedence and conditional-write limits.

Alternatively, enable the tool manually in the server configuration used by that host:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "experimental": { "todo": true }
}
```

Ask the agent in ordinary chat to create or change the list through `todowrite`.
Navigator displays the latest completed native call before the session's revert
boundary, reacts to host updates, and offers All / Active / Finished filters,
status groups, progress, Refresh, and retry after read failures. It does not start
model requests from Todo controls. Running or failed writes leave the last
completed list visible; a completed write with an empty array clears it.
Native tasks have `content` and one of `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, or
`cancelled`; priorities remain unavailable in OpenCode 2's native schema.

![Disabled native Todo offers enablement](screenshots/84-native-todo-disabled.png)

![Review the server configuration change before enabling Todo](screenshots/86-native-todo-enable-preview.png)

The optional **server** half of Navigator is used for provider-native quotas and
read-only access to the previous Navigator Todo archive. Add it to the server
configuration only when those integrations are needed:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-navigator"]
}
```

For a local source installation, use the directory containing Navigator's
`server.js` in the `plugin` array. Keep the TUI package in `cli.json` as above;
the server configuration alone does not replace it. Restart OpenCode after
configuring both. OpenCode owns native Todo persistence and tool instructions;
the separate `navigator_todo_write` tool and Navigator Todo-instructions control
are retired. OpenCode 1.x continues to show its supported host Todo source.

Previous Navigator tasks stay in their original plugin-scoped storage. Their
existing RPC is now a read-only archive; it never replaces native history or
deletes the saved list. To inspect a previous session explicitly:

```sh
opencode api --standalone rpc.call --param rpcID=opencode-navigator.todo --param method=list --data '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_previous"},"location":{"directory":"/path/to/project"}}'
```

### Coverage

Run `bun run test:coverage` to measure the primary TUI and browser-conditioned
GUI unit/render suites separately. LCOV reports are written to
`coverage/tui/lcov.info` and `coverage/gui/lcov.info`; `coverage/summary.md` and
`coverage/summary.json` report each suite and their unique source-line union.
Shared lines count once and are covered when either suite executes them.

This is coverage of executable `src/` lines loaded by those suites, not every
source file in the repository. It excludes generated bundles, test fixtures,
dependencies and packaged-host smoke runs. These Bun LCOV reports do not provide
branch coverage. The separate host checks remain mandatory. Coverage is
reporting-only; no minimum threshold or additional status gate is enabled.

CI retains the reports for 14 days as the `unit-coverage` artifact and adds the
line summary to the check job's summary on pushes, pull requests and submitted
reviews. The coverage link above opens those CI runs; it is not a separate
pass/fail or percentage badge. No external coverage account, upload token,
OIDC permission or automated PR comment is needed.

`bun run screenshots` builds a pinned Linux ARM64 image and captures the real TUI
through Ghostty on Xvfb. The image includes the bundled corner font and a pinned
JetBrainsMono Nerd Font; every displayed task, session, workspace, path, skill,
server, error, and preset is synthetic. `bun run screenshots:verify` renders the
same scenes to a temporary directory and fails if any PNG differs. Additional scenes
keep the pinned Nerd Font but remove the Navigator corner font so the uninstalled-font
experience remains reproducible beside the required-font captures. The harness
requires Docker with Linux ARM64 support. These commands are available for harness
development; committed release captures are generated by the `Prepare Release`
stage of the manually launched `Release` GitHub Actions workflow.

That workflow also runs `bun run screenshots:gui` and
`bun run screenshots:gui:verify`. They use the real packaged Desktop renderer on
Xvfb, not Ghostty, with synthetic sessions, providers and reports. The second run
compares the PNGs byte-for-byte. Fixed renderer and synthetic main clocks,
full software rasterization and disabled capture-time animations stabilize scenes
without stopping interaction timers or adding comparison tolerances. GUI
capture commands reject non-CI invocation; ordinary Desktop smoke tests never
take screenshots. Reproducible captures and the screenshot PR's required CI remain
pre-release gates; the release App does not need a manual PR approval.

## Publishing

Launch **Release** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) once on `main`, after merging
the package version and shipped changelog. No intermediate dispatch, workflow
approval, PR review or local publishing command is part of the release path:

1. Verify the release identity and independent review/CI rules, then run all seven
   mandatory checks on the exact source commit.
2. Call Prepare Release to capture both interfaces twice, create a PNG-only PR if
   needed, run its full CI and merge the exact generated head with the release App.
3. Run all seven checks again on the final `main` commit. A changed base or head
   stops the release instead of silently incorporating unrelated work.
4. Create the exact GitHub Release, wait for `Publish`, then verify registry
   integrity, signatures and provenance against its tag, commit and publishing run.

The release tag must match the package version, for example `v1.2.3` for `1.2.3`.
Do not republish after a timeout: inspect the existing GitHub Release and Publish
run first. Published versions are immutable; a mismatched existing tag is rejected.

### One-time release App setup

Register a private GitHub App owned by the repository owner and install it for
**this repository only**. Grant Contents, Pull requests and Actions read/write,
and Checks read-only. It needs no Administration, Workflows or user access.
Store its ID in the Actions variable `RELEASE_APP_ID` and its private key in the
Actions secret `RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`; never use the owner's personal token.
Short-lived installation tokens are narrowed per job and revoked afterwards.

Add that App as a **pull-request-only** bypass actor in the separate owner-review
ruleset. Keep `* @St1ggy` as the sole code owner and keep all seven required CI
checks, strict up-to-date enforcement and **no bypass actors** in the CI ruleset.
Ordinary contributor PRs still need owner review. The workflow verifies these
policies before doing release work. Do not add an approval-protected environment
to this unattended path. The App token is minted only after screenshot capture;
PR checks never receive it or an owner credential.

GitHub hides ruleset bypass lists from tokens without ruleset-write access. Do
not grant the App administrative writes just to inspect those lists. Once the
App exception is configured, run `bun scripts/release/audit-policy.ts` locally
with the already authenticated owner. It validates both policies and stores only
their server revisions and configuration in `RELEASE_POLICY_AUDIT`, an Actions
secret, without copying any owner credential. The release accepts a hidden list
only when the public rules and server revision still match that audit; unknown
or changed policies stop publication. Re-run the audit only after deliberately
changing a policy, not for every release.

The existing `publish.yml` uses npm Trusted Publishing with provenance. Configure
`St1ggy/opencode-navigator` and `publish.yml` as the trusted GitHub Actions
publisher in the package settings on npmjs.com before publishing a release.
The new npm package needs its own trusted-publisher configuration; the old
package's settings are not transferred by renaming the GitHub repository.

# Navigator corner font

`OpenCodeNavigatorCorners.ttf` is an original, MIT-licensed fallback font containing
rounded corner masks. It supplements the terminal's existing font.

| Code point | Corner |
| --- | --- |
| U+10F004 | Top-left cutout |
| U+10F005 | Top-right cutout |
| U+10F006 | Bottom-left cutout |
| U+10F007 | Bottom-right cutout |

The cell background fills the selection; glyphs paint only the outside corner in
the surrounding background color. This keeps multiline selections continuous even
when the terminal adds line spacing or rounds glyph bounds to fractional pixels.
The corner radius is one cell wide and no more than half a cell high.

Font version 1.001 adds these cutouts and retains U+10F000–U+10F003 as the original
filled corners for older plugin versions. Reinstall the font and fully restart the
terminal when upgrading from 1.000.

Generate the font with:

```sh
uv run scripts/generate-corner-font.py
uv run scripts/generate-corner-font.py --check
```

The generator pins FontTools and uses fixed timestamps for reproducible output.
Default metrics match IoskeleyMono Nerd Font Propo: 1000 units/em, 600-unit cell
width, ascender 965, descender -285. To match another terminal font's metrics:

```sh
uv run scripts/generate-corner-font.py --reference-font /path/to/terminal-font.ttf --output /tmp/OpenCodeNavigatorCorners.ttf
bun run font:install --source /tmp/OpenCodeNavigatorCorners.ttf
```

All corner outlines are generated from geometry; no outlines from the reference
font are copied. See the root `LICENSE` for the MIT license.

# Public Host APIs And Remaining Gaps

The compact Limits reset-time row uses the public Desktop Button and TUI sidebar
interaction controller for keyboard and mouse activation. Desktop 2.2.6 exports
neither a swap icon nor arbitrary Button style/ARIA props, so the native button
contains one small swap SVG, a clipped time label and a screen-reader action hint.
Replace only the SVG when a supported public swap icon becomes available; do not
replace the native button or reach into host DOM. Relative/absolute presentation
is local per quota-window identity and never invokes the quota adapter.

Quota gauge and clock glyphs are also absent from that public icon catalog;
small presentation-only SVGs cover those two symbols until the host exports them.
The provider display name comes from the selected server's public reactive
`data.location.provider.list(location)` cache, with the selected provider ID as
the loading fallback, and does not issue a quota request.

Navigator supports only OpenCode **1.19.5** and **2.2.6**, the current stable
release in each major line. Published SDK declarations and real-host checks
define the boundary; internal host components are not plugin APIs.

## Approved Desktop Integration Contract

Desktop support uses the independent `./gui-experimental` entry available from
Navigator 0.27.0, not the TUI entrypoint. Earlier packages do not include this GUI.
The approved target is OpenCode Desktop 2.2.6, with TUI 1.19.5 and 2.2.6 kept
behind explicit adapters. The published 2.2.6 plugin package preserves every TUI
declaration from 2.2.5; its changed declarations are GUI-specific.

| Capability | Published Desktop contract | Navigator integration constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GUI loading | `./gui-experimental`, `@opencode/plugin/gui`, one CJS bundle through `gui/vite` | Load from global server configuration; a CLI-only plugin entry does not enable Desktop. Preserve the server plugin's historical identity. |
| Data and requests | Reactive session `server.data` and live `server.client` | Resolve the selected session's server on every operation; the plugin-level client is the desktop sidecar, not an arbitrary remote session. |
| Session identity | Host session keys include server identity; location can be unavailable during reconnect | Partition domain state and reject stale actions by server/session/location; never put credentials in cache keys. |
| Layout | Native side panels, host-controlled bottom placement, narrow drawers, panel-specific width | Use native containers first. The optional floating view is an in-app presentation of the same state, not a detached OS window. |
| Commands and composer | Native command registry and reactive routed composer/model | Map verified commands explicitly; never emulate GUI actions by fabricating terminal command events. |
| Dialogs and settings | Native nested dialogs, SettingsPage and settings/menu components | Share validation and action state, not terminal dialog renderers or focus loops. |
| Local operations | Desktop main, validated IPC, Node/Electron only in main | Renderer models have no filesystem, subprocess or token access. Preserve the existing private store and lock rather than copying preferences to GUI storage. |
| Remote operations | The selected server's public client and existing plugin RPC | Do not read local project files or use local provider credentials for a remote target. Missing server capabilities remain explicit. |
| Native windows | Public main context can inspect existing windows; no panel detach operation | Detached OS windows are outside this delivery. Do not mutate host DOM or use private app internals to simulate support. |

The GUI API is experimental. Browser Web is not a verified target in this cycle.
The renderer and headless models must remain independent of Electron so a later
Web adapter does not require a second implementation of product rules.

Verification uses an npm-style tarball in the official checksum-verified Linux
ARM64 Desktop 2.2.6 package under Xvfb. Native macOS/Windows and multiple live
Desktop windows are not claimed as real-host coverage; remote identity, independent
window leases and concurrent shared-store writes are synthetic contracts. The
unminified TUI remains limited to 360,000 bytes; the single-file GUI has its own
600,000-byte budget (about 554 kB at the stage-10 baseline).

Native Settings temporarily has no mounted session and may have no active tab.
Navigator retains only a previously observed public session reference still
confirmed by the public tab list, server and location; Home, closing that tab or
changing its target clears it. Settings/profile operations use that reference's
live client/cache rather than substituting the sidecar.

Private favorites, trust, presets, account bindings and reset attempts remain in
the established filesystem preferences store/lock via typed main IPC. Native GUI
storage holds presentation only. Explicit Reload flushes writes, refreshes private
preferences and selected-server configured defaults, and clears temporary layout
overrides. Project profiles use the selected server RPC with exact file previews
and stale-file checks; workspace-placed filesystems are rejected until the public
server contract provides a verified placement-aware atomic write operation.

GUI permission actions open native Settings. No supported Desktop startup/Home
interception or LSP status contract was found; those terminal capabilities are not
simulated. Revisit the gaps when equivalent public APIs become available. Changelog
browsing is independent of the one-time version claim used by startup notes.

On narrow Desktop windows, Navigator uses **More → Navigator**, the host's
native drawer. The floating view redocks when the viewport becomes narrow.
Desktop 2.2.6 keeps drawer opening in its own mobile navigation; Navigator does
not click or move host elements to force it open. Revisit automatic drawer
opening when the public layout API exposes that operation.

GUI forms use `ctx.ui.Switch`, `TextInput`, `Select`, `Button` and the native
Settings rows rather than importing or bundling `@opencode/ui`. Desktop 2.2.6's
public UI facade has no multiline input, progress bar, disclosure row, or bookmark
icon. Those focused semantic controls remain plugin-owned, using the host theme's
surface, text, focus and elevation tokens. Remove these fallbacks when equivalent
public controls preserve their multiline, expanded/selected and progress semantics.

Reset-credit cards are semantic list-item layouts with host-themed borders; the
public facade has no generic card component. Their actions, detail disclosure and
icons use public `Ui.Button` and `Ui.Icon`. Expiry progress keeps the existing

uses its internal Tabs root, List, Trigger and Content components. They are not
exported by the plugin UI facade. Navigator therefore composes its category
navigation from public small neutral/ghost-muted Buttons, matching its Todo filters,
without importing the private Tabs module or copying the host DOM. Settings panels
mount on first visit and remain hidden rather than unmounting on category changes,
preserving drafts. Settings search passes the public `SettingsPage.render.target`

wrapper when public tabs support selection, keyboard navigation and retained panels.

### Dependency audit limits

The candidate's frozen install and peer graph pass, but its security audit is
not clean. The supported 1.x plugin pins an older Effect beta and Zod; its Effect

### Selected-server quota services

Desktop Codex reads and reset submissions run behind typed main-process IPC,
only for the host-verified `sameMachine` sidecar. Main rechecks the session
directory, live client, active connection and private account binding; it never
returns credentials or provider headers to the renderer. Remote sessions use
their selected server's quota RPC and never borrow the Desktop's local account.
Public session and quota-event locations expose only a directory, not a workspace
ID. Workspace requests retain explicit location guards, and quota observations
without sufficient workspace identity do not trigger an automatic read.

The ordinary Codex bucket is account-scoped even when `normalModelSlug` is null.
Missing reset-credit details do not erase the provider's available count. Reset
submission requires a separate confirmation and an authoritative persisted
attempt; uncertain retries retain its idempotency key. No credit is spent during
review, refresh or account linking.

# Provider Quota Sources

Navigator follows the currently selected host model and active provider connection.
It never treats session token/cost totals as remaining provider quota. Subscription
windows, API rate limits, configured capacities, and monetary balances are different
measurements and are labelled separately.

The experimental Desktop entry shares quota normalization, refresh scheduling,
account binding and reset-attempt rules with TUI. Its renderer uses the selected
session's live server client/cache. Local Codex subprocess access is restricted to
typed Desktop-main IPC for a host-verified same-machine connection; remote or
unverified targets never borrow the Desktop's local account or binding. No tokens
or credential files are returned to the renderer. Remote provider reads use the
selected server's existing quota RPC. Missing capabilities and authentication
failures remain explicit rather than enabling an alternate credential reader.

The external provider contracts were rechecked on 2026-10-06; the public
OpenCode Console/Go contract was added on 2026-10-28. The runtime also includes providers from
the host catalog; an unrecognized provider gets an explicit unverified-source state
rather than fabricated quota values. Availability depends on the selected account,
permissions, region, transport, and supported host APIs.

## Authentication And Host Boundaries

- OpenCode 2 metadata matching uses public provider/credential APIs and the built-in
  ChatGPT OAuth `metadata.accountID`. Account IDs are compared with Codex's own
  reported identity; a provider name or model-name similarity is not proof.
- ChatGPT token-sharing OAuth is recognized, but its `metadata.clientID` is not an
  account ID. Without `accountID`, explicitly confirm the Codex account link once
  per connection. The displayed quotas belong to that Codex account, not a separately
  verified token-sharing allowance.
- A confirmation is saved once per connection, or per provider when the host has
  no connection API. Models do not need separate confirmations. Conflicting older
  model-specific records remain isolated until an explicit relink.
- Additional read-only sources use Navigator's OpenCode 2 server plugin and public
  integration/HTTP-response hooks. Secrets remain on the server and are never
  returned by quota RPCs, written to Navigator preferences, or included in logs.
- Native response observations do not issue extra model requests. No quota read
  triggers inference, a credit purchase, a reset, or an authorization flow.
- HTTP-only observations may be absent for WebSocket transports. Report that
  limitation instead of changing the host transport or reading private frames.
- Console/Go use the host client API directly; other native provider adapters use
  the OpenCode 2 server plugin. OpenCode 1.x keeps Codex support and capability
  guidance without accessing host internals.
- REST credentials are not reused against a native provider origin when the host
  explicitly configures a different gateway origin. Redirects are rejected.
- Contract fixtures cover endpoint selection, regions, units, pagination, account
  ambiguity/rotation, malformed bodies, cancellation, and partial-data handling.
  These are deterministic checks, not live billing-account probes.
- Documentation from reference implementations is used only to discover APIs;
  browser cookies, credential-file readers, private endpoints, and organization-
  specific stacks are excluded.
